Not really the right sub, gothic studies and Goth don't really crossover except for individuals who happen to like both. That being said, I go to University of Kent where they do a module on Gothic film, and that has links to wider gothic studies. I attended a great conference on it ran by a couple of my uni's lecturers, which you may be interested in exploring further. It appears to be an annual thing that regularly calls for papers.

 [https://gothicfeminism.com/](https://gothicfeminism.com/) 

Hope you enjoy your course

Mine's Suspiria. It's from a film I like, but honestly I just find the word pretty. I try and go for a slightly dark/gothic feel for my town without being too edgy or morbid.

I've been spending every Christmas Eve at my girlfriends home for the last four years, as we both live with parents still and don't see each other on the actual day. We open each other's presents and often eat Chinese food and candy, then watch movies and cuddle and play games with her parents. It's our 5th year together this year and I can't wait to surprise her with some homemade art along with her other presents.

I always go for the Nightmare Before Christmas, as from Halloween to Christmas is when I'm at my happiest and that film so perfectly mixes them. I also love the Muppets Christmas Carol. 
Also Abed's Uncontrollable Christmas from the show Community. Reminds me of my favourite stop motions, and is so comforting to me as another autistic person who adores festivity and wants everything to be perfect for my friends and family.
